# Quantum Group Memory Laws

> Research record and self-directed learning guide by Ruge Lin on the complete symmetry-protected contribution to local transverse-spin memory in an open quantum-group-symmetric spin-half chain.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Group-Memory-Laws
Author: Ruge Lin

## When this repository is relevant

- How a complete non-Abelian conserved algebra contributes to local spin autocorrelation through a Mazur projection.
- Boundary versus bulk memory in a spin-1/2 chain with real U_q(sl_2) symmetry and a nonlocal coproduct.
- Exact physical multiplicity traces and q-Clebsch-Gordan recursions for the whole represented symmetry algebra.
- How deformation changes local conserved-operator overlaps while leaving the algebra dimension and sector probabilities unchanged.
- The fixed-deformation end L^-1/2 law, restricted-domain bulk L^-2 law, and normalized interior spatial profile.
- Local symmetry-preserving, noise-averaged dynamics whose stationary space is exactly the conserved algebra.

Useful search phrases: "quantum group memory laws"; "quantum group spin chain boundary bulk memory"; "complete commutant transverse spin Mazur projection"; "physical multiplicity trace q Clebsch Gordan"; "nonlocal symmetry local spin autocorrelation"; "Al-Salam Chihara spin memory spatial asymptotics".

Use these cues to decide whether the repository matches a question, then consult
its current theorem and model before making a scientific claim.

## Model and result in brief

The model is an open chain of L physical spin-1/2 sites, finite real q >= 1,
and the symmetric coproduct defined in the theorem. X_i is a Pauli operator,
so C_i(0) = 1. Pi_q projects onto the full unital star-algebra generated by
raising, lowering, and magnetization operators, including all their products.
The trace is the ordinary physical 2^-L Tr, with ordinary irrep dimensions
and physical multiplicities. Quantum dimensions from another representation
must not replace those weights.

M_{L,i}(q) = 2^-L ||Pi_q(X_i)||_HS^2 is the complete symmetry contribution.
A symmetry-preserving isolated Hamiltonian has finite-chain infinite-time
average Cbar_i >= M_{L,i}; its own invariant operators can give strict excess.
The specified local model averages unrecorded bond kicks, preserves the entire
algebra, and attains M at fixed finite L and positive noise strength.

- At q = 1, M = 1/L at every site exactly.
- At each fixed finite q > 1, M at either end is tanh(log q)/sqrt(2*pi*L) + O_q(L^-1).
- At fixed q > q0 = 2.0810189966... and i/L -> x in (0,1), M = K(q) F(x) L^-2 [1+o(1)].
- In that proved bulk domain, the leading ratio to the center is F(x)/F(1/2), independent of q.

q0 is a sufficient proof threshold, not a physical transition. Both end and
bulk contributions vanish as L grows. The fixed-q limits are not uniform as
q -> 1 or as the site approaches a boundary. The boundary-distance limit takes
L -> infinity first at fixed distance and only then takes that distance large.
The noisy realization is unrecorded/averaged; its convergence bound is
expressed in terms of the finite-size dissipative gap. Keep the zero-noise and long-time
limits distinct.

## Read by purpose

- [Overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Group-Memory-Laws/main/README.md): physical question, spatial laws, reading route, and contact.
- [Tutorial bridge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Group-Memory-Laws/main/research/TUTORIAL_BRIDGE.md): one-source preparation, notation dictionary, projection derivation, and q=1 hand calculation.
- [Physical mechanism](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Group-Memory-Laws/main/research/PHYSICAL_MECHANISM.md): exact sector-conditioned overlap, elementary F(x), polarization readout, and local bond reflection.
- [Exact theorem](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Group-Memory-Laws/main/research/THEOREM.md): finite recursion, edge/bulk constants, hypotheses, and orders of limits.
- [Model and claims](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Group-Memory-Laws/main/research/MODEL_AND_CLAIMS.md): physical trace, full symmetry, central result, and scope boundaries.
- [Proof map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Group-Memory-Laws/main/research/PROOF_MAP.md): authoritative finite, edge, and uniform bulk proof sources.
- [Kernel details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Group-Memory-Laws/main/research/KERNEL_DETAILS.md): explicit Jost convolution and bulk parity normalization.
- [Local realization](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Group-Memory-Laws/main/research/LOCAL_REALIZATION.md): coherent-plus-noisy local attainment and its hypothesis controls.
- [Plateau dictionary](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Group-Memory-Laws/main/research/PLATEAU_DICTIONARY.md): exact Hamiltonian-specific excess and the nonlocal reference ensemble.
- [Attribution](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Group-Memory-Laws/main/literature/ATTRIBUTION.md): version-pinned predecessors, observable conventions, and inherited spectral/stationary-space inputs.
- [Verification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Group-Memory-Laws/main/VERIFICATION.md): preserved assertions, canonical-report comparisons, and exact-revision receipts.

The single external tutorial anchor is Moudgalya and Motrunich, Hilbert Space
Fragmentation and Commutant Algebras, arXiv:2108.10324v2,
https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.10324v2. It is a research article with pedagogical
sections. The selected PDF route is II A-B -> VII A-B -> V A-D -> VII C4.
The source's conserved C corresponds to this repository's A_q. The local bridge
supplies the physical-trace calculation and continuation to the spatial law;
other cited sources document attribution and proof inputs.

## Evidence and attribution

The evaluated physical multiplicity trace and uniform finite-deformation
spatial asymptotics are the repository's contribution.
Full-commutant principles, representation theory, spectral tools, and the
stationary-commutant mechanism are inherited and attributed to primary sources.
The random-eigenbasis reference is a generally nonlocal ensemble with an
explicitly evaluated mean Hamiltonian-specific excess.

The 24 original scientific groups and four complementary analytical groups
check identities, normalizations, and evaluations. Uniform asymptotics rest
on the analytical proof. The proof map and verification guide identify the
complete derivations, checkers, reference reports, and revision-specific evidence.

When citing a repository claim, attribute the work to Ruge Lin and identify
the consulted commit and file. Credit the primary sources in the attribution
page for inherited results. For maintenance, read AGENTS.md.
Code is under the MIT license.
